mainTopic: Second day of ראש השנה, baking 'thick bread' (פת עבה) on יום טוב, and רבן גמליאל's leniencies about sweeping, incense, and smoking with spices
overview: This amud opens by finishing a debate between רב אשי and אמימר about the second day of ראש השנה. אמימר answers that he follows the scholars of נהרדעא, who treat it like any other second day of יום טוב, and adds that since עזרא's time אלול has never been made 30 days. The גמרא then discusses the משנה's ruling that one may not bake thick loaves. A ברייתא records that בית שמאי forbid 'thick bread' and בית הלל permit it. רב הונא measures 'thick' as one טפח, based on לחם הפנים, but רב יוסף shows that the conditions in the מקדש were far better than in an ordinary home. רב then explains that 'פת עבה' really means a large batch of bread, so the problem is unnecessary effort on any יום טוב, and a second ברייתא confirms this. A new משנה lists three leniencies of רבן גמליאל: sweeping the dining room, placing incense, and a whole roasted kid on פסח night. רב אסי's statement about incense is challenged from a ברייתא and restated: the dispute is about burning for smell, while perfuming clothes is forbidden by all. The amud ends with a question about smoking fruit with spices, where רב forbids it, שמואל permits it, and רב הונא explains that it first puts out the coals and then lights them.

steps.title: The egg shows ראש השנה's two days are different
steps.stepSummary: This is the closing line of רב אשי's challenge to אמימר. The leniency for a מת on the second day of ראש השנה does not carry over to an egg, so ראש השנה's second day is generally stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: …which is not so regarding an egg!
steps.whatsHappening: This amud begins in the middle of a challenge. The challenger finishes his point: the חכמים were lenient about burying a מת on the second day of ראש השנה, but that leniency does not apply to an egg laid on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a ביצה שנולדה ביום טוב, the two days of ראש השנה count as one long day of holiness. So an egg laid on day one stays forbidden on day two. That makes the second day of ראש השנה stricter than other second days, which is why אמימר's leniency is being questioned.

keyTerms.meaning: An egg, here an egg laid on יום טוב (the main topic of מסכת ביצה)
Which is not the case with…
The New Year festival, kept for two days even in ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the end of an argument that started on the previous amud. 'The egg' is shorthand for the rule that ראש השנה's two days form one continuous holiness, unlike the two days of other ימים טובים in חוץ לארץ.

phrases.english: which is not so with regard to an egg!
phrases.notes: Concludes the challenge: the burial leniency does not extend to the egg.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּבֵיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge begun on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's lenient treatment of the second day of יום טוב, as applied to ראש השנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second day of ראש השנה is part of one continuous holiness, as the egg law shows. So it should not be treated as leniently as other second days.

steps.title: אמימר follows נהרדעא, even regarding the egg
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that he holds like the scholars of נהרדעא. They treat the second day of ראש השנה like any other second day, even for the egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I hold like the scholars of נהרדעא, who say this even regarding an egg.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר defends himself by naming the opinion he follows. The scholars of נהרדעא say there is no difference between ראש השנה and other ימים טובים, even regarding the egg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's challenge assumed that everyone agrees the egg is forbidden on the second day of ראש השנה. אמימר removes that assumption. According to נהרדעא, the two days of ראש השנה are two separate days of holiness, just like other ימים טובים, so his leniency stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of נהרדעא, a major Babylonian Torah center
I hold / this is my opinion

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא כִּנְהַרְדָּעֵי סְבִירָא לִי,
phrases.english: He said to him: I hold like the scholars of Neharde'a,
who say [this] even with regard to an egg.
phrases.notes: Even for the egg, ראש השנה's two days are like other second days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא כִּנְהַרְדָּעֵי סְבִירָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adopting an opinion that rejects the challenger's premise
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees the egg law makes ראש השנה's second day stricter.
steps.terutzMaskana: נהרדעא treat the second day of ראש השנה like any other second day, even for the egg.

steps.title: Asking what the worry about ראש השנה really is
steps.stepSummary: אמימר asks his challenger what the basis for his concern is. Perhaps it is the worry that אלול will be made a 30-day month.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is your thinking? Perhaps they will make אלול a full month?
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר names the likely reason someone would be strict about the second day of ראש השנה. This question sets up his next move, where he will knock that reason down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בית דין made אלול 30 days long, the second day of ראש השנה would be the real א' תשרי. In that case it would be the true holiday and not a doubtful one. That is the logic behind treating it more strictly.

keyTerms.meaning: They will make it full (30 days) / extend it

phrases.english: And what is your reasoning?
phrases.notes: Opens the analysis of the challenger's concern.

phrases.english: Perhaps they will make Elul a full (30-day) month?
phrases.notes: If so, day two would be the real ראש השנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי דַּעְתָּיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אמימר's defense by identifying the reasoning behind the challenge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying reason for treating ראש השנה's second day more strictly

steps.title: אלול has not been extended since עזרא
steps.stepSummary: אמימר cites רב חיננא בר כהנא: from עזרא's time on, אלול has never been made a full month. So the worry is baseless.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב חיננא בר כהנא said: from the days of עזרא onward, we have not found a full אלול.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר brings a statement from an אמורא to prove that the worry from the last step does not exist in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since אלול is always 29 days, the first day of ראש השנה is always the real א' תשרי. The second day is then just a rabbinic addition, like other second days. Once the concern is gone, אמימר's leniency on the second day of ראש השנה is justified.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [so-and-so] say…? (introduces a contradicting or proving source)
From the days of עזרא and onward

steps.whatToRemember: אמימר follows נהרדעא: the second day of ראש השנה is like any other second day of יום טוב. He supports this from the fact that since עזרא's time, אלול has never been made 30 days.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that whether ראש השנה's second day is treated as one long day depends on whether there is a real doubt about the date. This idea comes up again in the הלכות of ראש השנה.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Ḥinnana bar Kahana say:
From the days of Ezra and onward
we have not found Elul made full.
phrases.notes: So there is no real doubt about the date of ראש השנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disproves the concern raised in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That the second day of ראש השנה need not be treated as the possible real holiday
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חיננא בר כהנא's historical statement that אלול has not been extended since עזרא

steps.title: משנה: only thin loaves may be baked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: one may not bake thick loaves on יום טוב, only thin ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not bake thick loaves, only thin ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the next ruling in the משנה, which it is about to discuss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is one of the three stringencies that רבן גמליאל taught, following בית שמאי. Baking thick loaves on יום טוב is forbidden, and only thin flat breads are allowed.
steps.confusionAlert: In the משנה, this ruling is a stringency of רבן גמליאל following בית שמאי. It is not the accepted view of בית הלל, as the next ברייתא shows.

phrases.english: And one may not bake thick loaves
but only thin ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין אוֹפִין פִּתִּין גְּרִיצִין אֶלָּא רְקִיקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: a return to the משנה after finishing the אמימר discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thick loaves may not be baked. Only thin ones may.

steps.title: ברייתא: בית שמאי and בית הלל on thick bread
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that בית שמאי forbid baking thick bread on פסח and בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: בית שמאי say one may not bake thick bread on פסח, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that shows the 'thick bread' issue is a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On פסח, the concern is that a thick dough might become חמץ before it finishes baking. בית שמאי are worried about this, while בית הלל allow it. This makes clear that the משנה's strict ruling follows בית שמאי.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: Beit Shammai say:
one may not bake thick bread on Passover,
phrases.notes: Concern that it may become חמץ.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא related to the משנה's ruling on thick loaves.
steps.raayaObject: That thick bread is a בית שמאי / בית הלל dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי forbid baking thick bread on פסח; בית הלל permit it.

steps.title: How thick is 'thick bread'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how thick a loaf must be to count as the 'thick bread' that בית הלל permit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is 'thick bread'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a measurement. This sets up רב הונא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used the term 'thick bread' without a size. To know how far בית הלל's permission goes, we need a measure.

phrases.english: And how much is thick bread?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה פַּת עָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define a term from the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The thickness that counts as 'thick bread'

steps.title: רב הונא: one טפח, like לחם הפנים
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the limit is one טפח, because לחם הפנים, which had to stay מצה, was one טפח thick.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: a טפח, for we find a טפח with לחם הפנים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question with a size and gives a source for it from the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לחם הפנים had to be מצה, and it was one טפח thick. So a טפח of thickness does not automatically become חמץ. רב הונא uses this to show that bread up to a טפח thick is safe on פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: The showbread in the מקדש, which was מצה

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: a handbreadth.
For we find with the showbread a handbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: טֶפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One טפח, derived from לחם הפנים

steps.title: רב יוסף rejects the comparison to לחם הפנים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives two reasons why לחם הפנים is not a fair model: the כהנים are extra careful, and that dough was very well kneaded. Ordinary bread made by ordinary people has neither advantage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: if they said this about careful people, would they say it about people who are not careful? If they said it about well-kneaded bread, would they say it about bread that is not well kneaded?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רב הונא's proof. He shows that לחם הפנים had special conditions that ordinary home baking does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the כהנים are זריזין, extra careful, so they make sure the dough does not become חמץ. Ordinary people are not as careful. Second, לחם הפנים was thoroughly kneaded, which slows down leavening, while ordinary bread is not. So a טפח that is safe for לחם הפנים may not be safe for regular bread.

keyTerms.meaning: If they said [it] here, would they say [it] there? (a 'not comparable' argument)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef strongly objected to it:
If they said it regarding diligent people,
would they say it regarding those who are not diligent?
If they said it regarding well-kneaded bread,
would they say it regarding bread that is not well kneaded?
phrases.notes: Ordinary bread is more likely to leaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's derivation in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's proof from לחם הפנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: לחם הפנים had two special safeguards: careful כהנים and thorough kneading. Ordinary bread lacks both, so the comparison does not hold.

steps.title: Three more differences between the Temple oven and a home oven
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף continues his challenge: the בית המקדש used dry wood, a hot oven, and a metal oven. Ordinary people use moist wood, a cooler oven, and an earthenware oven. So the bread of לחם הפנים is no model for everyday baking.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they said a טפח-thick loaf is fine when baked with dry wood, would they say the same with moist wood? If they said it for a hot oven, would they say it for a cool oven? If they said it for a metal oven, would they say it for a clay oven?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף keeps attacking רב הונא's proof from לחם הפנים. He lists three more ways the Temple's baking conditions were better than an ordinary person's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread that bakes slowly has more time to rise and become חמץ. Dry wood, a very hot oven, and a metal oven all bake fast, so a thick loaf in the בית המקדש stayed מצה. In a regular home, with moist wood and a clay oven, the same thickness could easily become חמץ.

phrases.english: If they said it regarding dry wood,
phrases.notes: Wood in the Temple was dry and burned hot.

phrases.english: would they say it regarding moist wood?
If they said it regarding a hot oven,
would they say it regarding a cool oven?
If they said it regarding a metal oven,
would they say it regarding an earthenware oven?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אָמְרוּ בְּעֵצִים יְבֵשִׁים — יֹאמְרוּ בְּעֵצִים לַחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יוסף's list of reasons from Step 9, adding three physical differences in baking conditions.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's proof from לחם הפנים that a טפח-thick loaf is safe from חמץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Temple's baking conditions (dry wood, hot oven, metal oven) were special. What stayed מצה there proves nothing about ordinary homes.

steps.title: Thick bread really means a large batch of bread
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא reports that he asked his teacher רב privately, and רב said 'פת עבה' means a large quantity of bread, not a thick loaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said: I asked my teacher privately (and who was it? רב): What is 'thick bread'? He answered: a large quantity of bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a completely new way to read the ברייתא. 'Thick bread' does not refer to how tall the loaf is but to how much bread is baked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes the whole debate about thickness and חמץ. If 'פת עבה' means a big batch, then בית שמאי forbid it because it is unnecessary effort on יום טוב, not because it may become חמץ. רב יוסף's objections to רב הונא no longer matter.
steps.confusionAlert: In this version, 'רבי' means 'my teacher' and refers to רב, not to רבי יהודה הנשיא. The גמרא asks 'ומנו' precisely to clarify who is meant.
steps.whyThisMatters: It changes the topic of the ברייתא from a חמץ concern to a concern about unnecessary effort (טרחה) on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said:
I asked my teacher in private,
and who is that? Rav:
phrases.notes: The גמרא identifies 'my teacher' as רב.

phrases.english: What is 'thick bread'?
A large quantity of bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁאֵלִית אֶת רַבִּי בְּיִחוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב יוסף undermined the thickness approach, a new definition of the term sidesteps the problem entirely.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'פת עבה' in the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It means a large quantity of bread, so the issue is excess effort, not חמץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'פת עבה' means a large quantity of bread (the concern is unnecessary effort, not חמץ).

steps.title: Another version: רב learned it from רבינו הקדוש
steps.stepSummary: Some say the chain of transmission was one level higher: רב ירמיה בר אבא quoted רב, who had asked his own teacher, רבינו הקדוש, privately. The answer is the same: a large quantity of bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of רב: I asked my teacher privately (and who was it? רבינו הקדוש): What is 'thick bread'? A large quantity of bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of who said the teaching. The content stays the same; only the speaker changes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the definition 'large quantity of bread' comes from רבי יהודה הנשיא himself, the editor of the משנה. That gives the explanation even more weight.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:
I asked my teacher in private,
and who is that? Our holy Rabbi:
phrases.notes: Here 'my teacher' is רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: What is 'thick bread'?
A large quantity of bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel version of Step 11 that differs only in the chain of transmission.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'פת עבה' means a large quantity of bread, as taught by רבינו הקדוש.

steps.title: Why call a big batch 'thick'?
steps.stepSummary: If the term means a large quantity, why does the ברייתא use the word 'thick'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do they call it 'thick bread'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a wording question about the new explanation. This sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Thick' normally describes size or height, not amount. So the גמרא needs to justify reading the word as 'a lot of bread'.

phrases.english: And why do they call it 'thick bread'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי קָרוּ לֵיהּ פַּת עָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording behind the definition given in Steps 11–12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a large quantity of bread would be described as 'thick'.

steps.title: Two reasons for the name 'thick bread'
steps.stepSummary: Either a large batch of dough swells up a lot during kneading and looks thick, or in the תנא's region people simply called a large batch 'thick bread'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it swells up a lot during kneading. Alternatively, in this תנא's place, a large quantity of bread was called 'thick bread'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with two possible explanations of the name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer is physical: a big mass of dough looks thick while being kneaded. The second answer is linguistic: it was simply the local way of speaking where this תנא lived.

phrases.english: Because it is greatly expanded in the kneading.
Alternatively, in the place of this tanna,

phrases.aramaic: פַּת מְרוּבָּה — פַּת עָבָה קָרוּ לֵיהּ
phrases.english: a large quantity of bread they called 'thick bread'.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דִּנְפִישָׁא בְּלִישָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A big batch swells during kneading, or 'thick bread' was the local term for a large batch.

steps.title: If the problem is effort, why mention only פסח?
steps.stepSummary: If the ban is about unnecessary effort, it should apply on every יום טוב. So why did the ברייתא mention פסח specifically?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, since the reason is that he takes on effort he does not need, why mention פסח specifically? It should apply on the other ימים טובים too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from Step 6 based on the new explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mentioning פסח made sense when the worry was חמץ. Once the reason is unnecessary effort, nothing about it is special to פסח. So the ברייתא's focus on פסח looks out of place.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since (sets up a logical assumption)

phrases.english: Now, since it is because he exerts himself
with effort that is not needed,
why specifically Pesach?
Even on the other Festivals as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדִי מִשּׁוּם דְּקָטָרַח טִרְחָא דְּלָא צְרִיךְ הוּא, מַאי אִרְיָא פֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the new 'large quantity' explanation against the ברייתא's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's mention of פסח specifically.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An effort-based prohibition applies on all ימים טובים, so limiting it to פסח makes no sense.

steps.title: Yes, it applies on every יום טוב; the תנא was discussing פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees the rule applies on every יום טוב. The תנא mentioned פסח only because that was the topic he was teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so. But the תנא was dealing with the יום טוב of פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by agreeing with it. The mention of פסח was only context, not a limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule itself covers every יום טוב. The word 'פסח' in the ברייתא reflects what the תנא was discussing at the time. It is not a condition of the law.

keyTerms.meaning: He was standing in / dealing with

steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that the ban on a large batch is a פסח-only law. The גמרא says the opposite: it applies on every יום טוב.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so.
But the tanna was dealing with the Festival of Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes the point and explains the wording as context only.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mention of פסח limits the rule to פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies on all ימים טובים; פסח was simply the topic at hand.

steps.title: A ברייתא states the dispute for every יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports this: בית שמאי say one may not bake a large quantity of bread on יום טוב, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: בית שמאי say one may not bake a large quantity of bread on יום טוב, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports its answer. This version says 'יום טוב' in general and uses the clear phrase 'large quantity of bread'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא confirms both points at once. 'פת עבה' means 'פת מרובה', and the dispute applies on every יום טוב, not just פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught so (a supporting ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: 'פת עבה' in the ברייתא means a large batch of bread. בית שמאי forbid it on any יום טוב because of unnecessary effort, and בית הלל permit it. The mention of פסח was only because that was the topic.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹפִין פַּת מְרוּבָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One may not bake a large quantity of bread on a Festival,
and Beit Hillel permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 16 and the definition in Steps 11–12.
steps.raayaObject: That 'פת עבה' means a large quantity and that the dispute applies on every יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating the בית שמאי / בית הלל dispute about 'פת מרובה' on יום טוב in general.

steps.title: New משנה: Three leniencies of רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל permits three things: sweeping the dining room on יום טוב, placing incense on coals on יום טוב, and preparing a whole roasted kid on פסח night. The חכמים forbid all three.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: He (רבן גמליאל) also said three things to be lenient. One may sweep the room where people recline on couches to eat. One may place incense on coals on יום טוב. One may make a whole roasted kid goat on the nights of פסח. The חכמים forbid all three.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. After the previous משנה's three stringencies of רבן גמליאל, it lists three cases where he is lenient and the חכמים are strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "He also" points back to רבן גמליאל, who was quoted in the previous משנה. The חכמים have a separate reason for each case. Sweeping might lead a person to level holes in a dirt floor. Incense is not a normal food-preparation activity. A whole roasted kid on פסח night looks like eating a קרבן פסח outside the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: The dining room, where people reclined on couches
Incense: fragrant spices placed on hot coals
A kid goat roasted whole, the way the קרבן פסח was roasted

steps.confusionAlert: "אף הוא" (he also) does not mean a new person. It refers to רבן גמליאל from the previous משנה.

phrases.english: MISHNA: He, too, said
three things to be lenient:
one may sweep the room of the couches,
and one may place incense on a Festival,
and one may make a whole roasted kid goat
on the nights of Passover.
And the Sages forbid.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אַף הוּא אָמַר שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים לְהָקֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. After the previous משנה's three stringencies of רבן גמליאל, it lists three of his leniencies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל permits sweeping, incense, and a whole roasted kid on פסח night. The חכמים forbid all three.

steps.title: רב אסי: The incense dispute is only about perfuming
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי says the argument over incense is only about perfuming clothes. Using incense just to enjoy the smell is permitted by everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב אסי said: The argument is about burning incense to perfume (clothing). But burning it just to smell the fragrance is permitted according to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי narrows the incense part of the משנה. He tells us exactly which case the חכמים and רבן גמליאל argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Enjoying a smell is a bodily pleasure, so it counts like preparing food, which is allowed on יום טוב. Perfuming clothes is not a bodily need of that kind. Only that case is in dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: To perfume something, such as clothing, with incense smoke
To smell, to enjoy the fragrance

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the claim the rest of this passage will challenge.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Asi said:
The dispute is about perfuming (garments),
but to smell (the fragrance)
all agree it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי: מַחְלוֹקֶת לְגַמֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact case of the incense argument in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The incense argument is only about perfuming. Burning incense to enjoy the smell is permitted by all.

steps.title: Objection begins: A ברייתא on sweeping the dining room
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב אסי. It opens with the sweeping case: one may not sweep, but רבן גמליאל's household did sweep.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: One may not sweep the dining room on יום טוב. But in רבן גמליאל's house they did sweep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא to attack רב אסי. The sweeping part is the setup. The part about incense, which matters for the challenge, comes a few lines later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא goes through the משנה's cases one at a time. Each time it states the ruling and then what רבן גמליאל's house did. We need to see the whole pattern before the incense clause challenges רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection, usually from a ברייתא

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְכַבְּדִין בֵּית הַמִּטּוֹת בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One may not sweep the room of the couches on a Festival,
but those of Rabban Gamliel's house would sweep.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אֵין מְכַבְּדִין בֵּית הַמִּטּוֹת בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a ברייתא brought against רב אסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's claim that everyone permits incense for smelling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is the setup. The actual attack comes from the incense clause of the same ברייתא in step 23.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בר צדוק: They swept before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בר צדוק testifies that רבן גמליאל's house did not sweep on יום טוב. They swept the day before and covered the floor with sheets. On יום טוב they removed the sheets, and the room was already clean.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בר צדוק said: Many times I followed my father into רבן גמליאל's house. They did not sweep the dining room on יום טוב. Instead, they swept it on ערב יום טוב and spread sheets over it. The next day, when guests came in, they removed the sheets, and the house turned out to be clean on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, an eyewitness corrects the report about רבן גמליאל. He says no sweeping was actually done on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this testimony, the cleaning happened before יום טוב. The only thing done on יום טוב was lifting off the sheets. So רבן גמליאל's household did nothing questionable on יום טוב itself.

keyTerms.meaning: On its own, without any new action

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer bar Tzadok said:
Many times I entered following Father,
into Rabban Gamliel's house,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיוּ מְכַבְּדִין בֵּית הַמִּטּוֹת בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: and they would not sweep the room of the couches on a Festival,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מְכַבְּדִין אוֹתָן מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: rather they would sweep them on the eve of the Festival,
and spread sheets over them.
The next day, when guests would enter,
they would remove the sheets,
and the house turned out to be clean on its own.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּר צָדוֹק: פְּעָמִים הַרְבֵּה נִכְנַסְתִּי אַחַר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An eyewitness inside the ברייתא reinterprets what רבן גמליאל's house did.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל's household swept before יום טוב and only removed the covering sheets on יום טוב.

steps.title: The חכמים: That method would be allowed even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי אליעזר בר צדוק that his method is permitted even on שבת. So it cannot be the case the argument is about.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: If so, it is permitted to do this even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים react to the testimony. They point out that what he described is not the leniency under discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing sheets is not forbidden even on שבת, which is stricter than יום טוב. So it cannot be what "רבן גמליאל's house would sweep" refers to. The original report must mean real sweeping on יום טוב.

phrases.english: They said to him: If so,
even on Shabbat it is permitted to do so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אִם כֵּן, אַף בַּשַּׁבָּת מוּתָּר לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on רבי אליעזר בר צדוק's testimony.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the sheet method is the leniency of רבן גמליאל being discussed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The sheet method is permitted even on שבת, so there would be nothing to argue about.

steps.title: The ברייתא's incense clause: One may not place incense
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: one may not place incense on יום טוב, but רבן גמליאל's house did. This is the clause the גמרא will use against רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not place incense on coals on יום טוב. But in רבן גמליאל's house they did place it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reaches the incense case, which is the part that matters for the objection. The גמרא is setting up its challenge to רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids incense on יום טוב with no limits. Incense placed in a house for guests seems to be for its smell. Yet רב אסי said everyone permits incense for smelling. That tension drives the objection.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מַנִּיחִין אֶת הַמּוּגְמָר בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: And one may not place incense on a Festival,
but those of Rabban Gamliel's house would place it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מַנִּיחִין אֶת הַמּוּגְמָר בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, moving from sweeping to incense.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's claim that everyone permits incense for smelling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids incense in a setting that seems to be for the smell. That contradicts רב אסי's claim that smelling is permitted by all.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בר צדוק: The pans were filled with smoke before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בר צדוק testifies again. רבן גמליאל's house filled iron pans with incense smoke on ערב יום טוב and plugged their holes. On יום טוב they only opened the holes, and the house filled with fragrance on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בר צדוק said: Many times I followed my father into רבן גמליאל's house. They did not place incense on יום טוב. Instead, they brought perforated iron pans and filled them with incense smoke on ערב יום טוב. They plugged the holes on ערב יום טוב. The next day, when guests came in, they opened the holes, and the house turned out to be perfumed on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: In the incense clause, the same eyewitness again says nothing was actually done on יום טוב. The smoke was prepared beforehand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This testimony follows the same pattern as the sweeping case. The work was done before יום טוב, and on יום טוב they only uncovered the result. The house was perfumed so guests could enjoy the smell, which is why this clause seems to cut against רב אסי.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a clear pattern for both sweeping and incense. The ברייתא's ruling forbids the act on יום טוב. רבי אליעזר בר צדוק says רבן גמליאל's house did the work before יום טוב and only uncovered the result on יום טוב. The incense clause is the basis for the objection to רב אסי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer bar Tzadok said:

phrases.aramaic: פְּעָמִים הַרְבֵּה נִכְנַסְתִּי אַחַר אַבָּא לְבֵית רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: Many times I entered following Father into Rabban Gamliel's house,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיוּ מַנִּיחִין אֶת הַמּוּגְמָר בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: and they would not place incense on a Festival,
rather they would bring perforated pans made of iron
and fill them with smoke from the eve of the Festival,
and plug their holes on the eve of the Festival.
The next day, when guests would enter,
they would open their holes,
and the house turned out to be perfumed on its own.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּר צָדוֹק: פְּעָמִים הַרְבֵּה נִכְנַסְתִּי אַחַר אַבָּא לְבֵית רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An eyewitness reinterprets the incense practice of רבן גמליאל's house, in parallel to step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל's household prepared the incense smoke before יום טוב and only opened the pans on יום טוב.

steps.title: The חכמים reject the incense report because it would be allowed even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reply to רבי אליעזר בר צדוק that his incense method is permitted even on שבת. So his story cannot be what the ברייתא's argument is about. This leaves the challenge against רב אסי standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: If so, it would be permitted to do that even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי אליעזר בר צדוק, just as they did with the sweeping case. If רבן גמליאל's house only opened holes in pre-filled pans, there is nothing even close to forbidden, even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the sealed-pan method would be permitted even on שבת, the case under dispute must be actually placing incense on coals on יום טוב. That burning was done to make the house smell nice for guests, which is smell, not perfuming clothes. So the חכמים forbid burning for smell, and this goes against the earlier version of רב אסי that said everyone allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the other חכמים) said to him
If so (if that is what happened)

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying that burning incense is allowed on שבת. They are saying that רבי אליעזר בר צדוק's method of just uncovering holes would be allowed even on שבת, so it cannot be the case they are arguing about.

phrases.english: They said to him:
If so,
even on Shabbat it is permitted to do so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אִם כֵּן, אַף בַּשַּׁבָּת מוּתָּר לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי אליעזר בר צדוק's report in step 24, which completes the challenge to רב אסי begun in step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי אליעזר בר צדוק's description as the case under dispute.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His method involves no יום טוב act at all, since it is permitted even on שבת, so it cannot be what the חכמים forbade.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier version of רב אסי, which allowed burning incense for smell according to everyone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The disputed case was burning for house fragrance, which is smell, and the חכמים forbade it.

steps.title: The corrected version of רב אסי's statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the earlier version of רב אסי. It says that if he said anything, he said this: the argument is about burning incense for smell, but burning to perfume clothes is forbidden by all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said. רב אסי said: The dispute is about burning for smell, but burning to perfume clothes is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: Because the ברייתא disproved the earlier version, the גמרא restates רב אסי's words so they fit the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the new version, smell is the case under debate, which matches the ברייתא where the חכמים forbade house fragrance. Perfuming clothes is not a bodily enjoyment at all, so it cannot be compared to food preparation, and everyone forbids it. The challenge is answered by flipping which case is disputed.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said (the גמרא retracts and restates)
To smell (burning incense to enjoy the fragrance)

steps.whatToRemember: Final version of רב אסי: the argument is only about burning for smell. Perfuming clothes is forbidden by everyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the conclusion of the incense discussion: perfuming clothes on יום טוב is forbidden according to all opinions.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated,
it was stated like this:
Rav Asi said:
The dispute is about burning for smell,
but to perfume garments, it is prohibited.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אִי אִתְּמַר הָכִי אִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge completed in step 25 by restating רב אסי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reformulation (the statement is restated in a different version)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אסי held that burning for smell is allowed by all, and the dispute is about perfuming.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about smell, and perfuming garments is forbidden by all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burning incense to perfume clothes on יום טוב is forbidden by everyone.

steps.title: New question: may one smoke fruit with spices on יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: A new question is raised: what is the law about smoking fruit with spices on יום טוב to give it a nice smell?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: What is the law about smoking (fruit with spice smoke)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about smoking, which sets up the opinions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is different from the incense case, because here the smoke is meant to improve food. That might make it count as food preparation, which is allowed on יום טוב. The question is whether that is enough to permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them
To smoke (fruit or food with spice smoke, to add fragrance)

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
What is the law with regard to smoking?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לְעַשֵּׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from incense for smell or clothing to a related case involving food.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether smoking fruit with spices on יום טוב is allowed.

steps.title: רב forbids smoking, שמואל permits it
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא reports in the name of רב that smoking is forbidden. שמואל says it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of רב: It is forbidden. And שמואל said: It is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with two opposite opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that adding fragrance does not count as allowed food preparation. שמואל holds that it does count, since it improves the food. No reason is given yet, and the next step supplies one for the forbidding side.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:
It is prohibited.
And Shmuel said: It is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב: אָסוּר. וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 27.

steps.title: רב הונא: forbidden because it puts out the coals
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that smoking is forbidden, because sprinkling spices on the coals puts some of them out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: It is forbidden, because he puts out (the coals).
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a specific reason for forbidding smoking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When powdered spices land on burning coals, they put out part of the fire. Putting out a fire is a מלאכה (כיבוי), and it is not needed for the food, so it is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: It is prohibited,
because he extinguishes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: אָסוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמְּכַבֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a reason for forbidding smoking, siding with the forbidding view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Smoking with spices is forbidden because of putting out the coals.

steps.title: רב נחמן: why not say it is forbidden because it lights the fire?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks רב הונא why he chose putting out as the reason. The spices also make the coals burn more, which is lighting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: Let the master say instead that it is forbidden because he lights (the fire)!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן questions the reason רב הונא chose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the spices land, they catch fire and make the coals burn stronger, which is הבערה. רב נחמן suggests that this is the more obvious problem. So why focus on putting out the fire?

keyTerms.meaning: Let the master say (a suggestion phrased as a challenge)

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said to him:
And let the Master say: because he kindles?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: וְנֵימָא מָר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּבְעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's reason of putting out the fire.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The spices also feed the fire, so lighting seems an equal or better reason, and naming only putting out looks incomplete.

steps.title: רב הונא: first it puts out, then it lights
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that both happen. At the start the spices put out the coals, and afterwards they make the coals burn.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: At its beginning it puts out, and at its end it lights.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא accepts רב נחמן's point and explains that both problems are present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא mentioned putting out the fire because it happens first, the moment the spices touch the coals. Lighting comes afterwards. So the act involves two forbidden actions, one after the other.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Its beginning is extinguishing
and its end is kindling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תְּחִלָּתוֹ מְכַבֶּה וְסוֹפוֹ מַבְעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge from step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both reasons apply (they happen in sequence)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only putting out the fire was the issue, so lighting was being ignored.
steps.terutzMaskana: Putting out happens first and lighting follows, so both are involved.

steps.title: רב יהודה: on a burning coal it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that sprinkling spices directly on a burning coal is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: On top of a coal, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a practical ruling about where the spices are placed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting spices right on a burning coal brings in the problems of putting out and lighting the fire described above. By saying 'on a coal,' רב יהודה limits the prohibition to that specific setup.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
On top of a coal, it is prohibited.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: עַל גַּבֵּי גַּחֶלֶת אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the putting-out and lighting concern to a specific practical case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Placing spices directly on a burning coal on יום טוב is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: Smoking with spices: רב forbids it and שמואל permits it. רב הונא's reason is putting out, then lighting. רב יהודה rules that directly on a coal it is forbidden.
